newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: SENATOR COLSTON DISCHARGED FROM HOSPITAL
Senator Mal Colston has left the Brisbane hospital where he has spent the last week recovering from pnemonia and other medical complaints.
The Senator left under the cover of darkness late last night.
He is currently convalescing at an undisclosed location.
The hospital says Senator Colston is feeling very well and he also extended his thanks for the courtesy provided by many of the media.
FARMERS REJECT ABORIGINAL POSITION ON NATIVE TITLE
The National Farmers' Federation says the Aboriginal negotiator's proposal on native title ignores the 1993 agreement for extinguishment of native title on pastoral leases.
Indigenous leaders yesterday presented their solution to the Wik debate, agreeing to confirm pastoralists' existing rights, but not to upgrade them.

Chairman of the NFF's Aboriginal Affairs Task Force, John Mackenzie, says the Aboriginal proposal doesn't provide the certainty pastoralists need, and doesn't take into account today's business realities.
MANUFACTURERS LOBBY GREATER PLACE IN THE ECONOMY
The Australian Chamber of Manufactures is planning to lift manufacturing to 15 per cent of the national economy by the year 2010.
The chamber says the Federal Government is being lobbied to develop strategies for both export and import replacement industries.
Victorian regional manager, Craig Rutledge, says growth and prosperity in the manufacturing sector will lead to more jobs, particularly in country areas.
DANGEROUS DOG DEFINITION TOO NARROW SAYS EXPERT
An expert on dog behaviour wants the definition of a dangerous dog broadened in Victoria following a fatal dog attack on a 12-year old boy last night.
Jarred Dwyer died in the backyard of his Meadow Heights home after being attacked by a dog.
Dr Graeme Smith from the Melbourne Lost Dogs Home says under the year-old Domestic Animals Act a dog has to cause serious injury requiring stitches before it's defined as dangerous.
But Dr Smith says most dog attacks cause bruising.
He says only about 100 of Victoria's three-quarters-of-a-million dogs, have been declared dangerous since the Act was introduced.
JOB PROSPECTS SET TO IMPROVE: SURVEY
A survey of employers' hiring intentions indicates employment is expected to rise by point-four per-cent in the April-June quarter.
Nine out of 13 sectors interviewed by Drake International anticipated real increases in staffing levels.
The survey found most job prospects are in information technology, business services, and the retail sector.
The employment of non-permanent staff is increasing with more than one in three of jobs in the June quarter expected to go to casual and contract workers.
Victoria remains the nation's top employer.
Prospects for most states are better than for the previous three months, but are down on the same period last year.
AUSSIE SQUAD TO DEFEND THE ASHES NAMED
Australia's Cricket selectors have recalled Ricky Ponting and Michael Slater to the 17 strong squad to defend the Ashes in the six test series against England.
As expected they have stuck with Mark Taylor as captain, however Steve Waugh has replaced Ian Healy as vice captain.
The rest of the squad is Bevan, Bichel, Blewett, Elliott, Gilchrist, Gillespie, Julian, Kasprowicz, Langer, McGrath, Warne and Mark Waugh.
The four month tour starting in May also includes three one day internationals.
